display.title: Episode 470: Saved by a Miracle, Chapter 2 (Before Pesach)
display.summary_short: Uncle Yossi prepares children for Pesach: matzah, the Seder and inviting guests, Shema with a Beis Yaakov class, and the end of a story of the Alter Rebbe's puzzling advice that saved a life.
display.summary_long: A pre-Pesach broadcast from 5751. Uncle Yossi explains that Pesach is the holiday of our freedom, which we relive at the Seder by reading the Haggadah and eating matzah, and gives the dates of the Sedarim. The order of the day: invite a relative or friend who has no Seder of their own, just as the Haggadah opens with 'Let all who are hungry come and eat.' After the Hakochainik march, a first-grade class from Beis Yaakov of Boro Park recites the Shema, and everyone gives tzedakah. Story time concludes the tale Uncle Yossi calls 'Through the Eyes of a Tzaddik': Reb Boruch, framed by a jealous co-worker for stealing logs, follows the Alter Rebbe's instruction to wait a full week before seeing the minister, and discovers that the delay saved his life and cleared his name. The program closes with practical guidance on not eating or owning chametz, the search and burning of chametz, and selling chametz through a rabbi.
display.lesson: What looks puzzling to us can be clear through the eyes of a tzaddik; trust Hashem and follow a tzaddik's guidance. Before Pesach, share your Seder with someone who has none.

date.note: Gives Pesach 5751 dates (first Seder Friday night 29 March 1991; bedikas chametz 28 March). Episode 472 states Yud-Aleph Nissan (Tuesday 26 March 1991), so 470 is two weeks earlier.

advisories.note: The minister reveals that Reb Boruch was to be shot on sight had he come on the original day.

privacy.note: A visiting class's teacher is named on air.
